title: Separation Techniques
seo_title: Secondary 1 Science: Separation Techniques Worksheets (Lower Secondary Science with Answers)
standard_code: Secondary 1: Exploring Diversity of Matter using Separation Techniques
standard_text: Explain how magnetic attraction, filtration, evaporation, distillation and paper chromatography separate the parts of a mixture and investigate the principles behind them; describe their uses in water treatment (filtration, distillation, reverse osmosis), food safety and waste management, and appreciate Singapore's sustainable supply of potable water (summary of the MOE Lower Secondary Science Syllabus).
meta_desc: Free Secondary 1 science worksheets for Singapore students on separation techniques: filtration, evaporation, distillation, chromatography, magnets, NEWater and desalination. With answers.
key_big: Separate mixtures by their different properties.
key_sub: Insoluble solid: filter. Dissolved solid: evaporate. Pure liquid: distil.
body_html:
How to think about it

Mixtures can be separated because their parts have different physical properties.

  • Magnetic attraction: magnetic from non-magnetic. Filtration: insoluble solid from a liquid.
  • Evaporation: a dissolved solid from its solvent. Distillation: a pure liquid from a solution, by boiling and condensing.
  • Paper chromatography: the dyes in a mixture, because they travel different distances.
  • Singapore's water: local catchment, imported water, NEWater and desalinated water (reverse osmosis).
Example

How do you separate sand from water?

Sand is insoluble

Answer: filtration

Example

How do you get pure water from sea water?

Boil and condense the water

Answer: distillation

Common mistakes

  • Using filtration to remove dissolved salt. Salt passes through filter paper.
  • Thinking distillation collects the solid. It collects the pure liquid.
  • Mixing up residue (stays on the paper) and filtrate (passes through).
  • Drawing the start line in ink. Use pencil; ink dissolves in the solvent.

items.q: In a separation experiment, which statement about the condenser is correct?
c: It is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.
It flows in at the bottom and out at the top so that the condenser stays full and cold.
It cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.
It make the liquid boil smoothly.
items.e: The condenser cools the vapour so that it condenses into a liquid.

items.e: The distillate is the pure liquid collected in the receiver.

items.q: What is the principle behind evaporation?
c: Insoluble solid particles are too big to pass through the tiny holes in the filter paper.
Only magnetic materials such as iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are attracted to a magnet.
The solvent changes into a gas and escapes, leaving the dissolved solid behind.
Different dyes have different solubilities in the solvent, so they travel different distances.
items.e: This is how evaporation works.

items.e: Boiling chips make the liquid boil smoothly.

items.q: 30 g of sugar dissolves completely in 200 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
items.e: Mass is conserved: 30 + 200 = 230 g. The solute is still there, just spread out.

items.q: 10 g of salt dissolves completely in 200 g of water. What is the mass of the solution?
